subject: SEO Update — ARLO — 2026-10-12
html:
Rank stayed flat for a 16th straight week (0 of 22 tracked keywords, avg position 100; backlinks flat 3/2 referring domains since 09-10) and catalog.ts/destinations/catalog.ts are both unchanged — shareable_dashboard's "October 2026" ETA still hasn't flipped, with under 3 weeks of the month left. CI stayed green: 50/50 SEO Report Email runs all-time. With FOCUS and the catalog both re-confirmed exhausted, this session closed out the follow-up promised by Thursday's (2026-10-08) session: it had audited about/blog/contact/pricing/compare for a stale clone-and-forget OG/JSON-LD bug but flagged the remaining static page shells as not yet given the same check. This session gave all 16 _shell.html files in the app a direct head-to-head audit and found one real instance of the same bug class.

PageWhat ChangedTarget KeywordCheck It
/destinations (the destinations hub page)Its JSON-LD WebPage breadcrumb named its own second level "ARLO" and pointed it back at the homepage, instead of naming it "Destinations" and pointing at itself — confirmed wrong against two correctly-built sibling patterns (the /compare hub, and the hub's own dynamic /destinations/[slug] template, both of which do Home → [Hub Name] → itself correctly). Fixed the hub's breadcrumb to match. The 6 services-persona page shells and the destinations template were also checked and found correct — no further instances of this bug class remain in any static shell.N/A — on-page/schema correctness fixaskarlo.app/destinations — view page source, find the second JSON-LD script tag's breadcrumb.itemListElement[1]

Next: watch shareable_dashboard's October ETA closely over the next 1-2 sessions — it's the one catalog entry due to flip this month, and the next real content opportunity once it does. Everything else (FOCUS cluster, connector matrix, comparison hub, destinations comparisons, blog) stays caught up against current demand; off-page Phase 1 (0/6), GSC submission, and the AI Result Tracker (zero LLM engines configured) remain the standing human-gated blockers.
